Stated Claim / Post Context:
Oberlin art professor and woman both found murdered in home on quiet Ohio street

The 64-year-old professor was found dead on the first floor, while his wife was on the second floor. Both the victims died of multiple gunshot wounds

Actual Article Body:
By ANANYA SWAROOP, US NEWS REPORTER

Published:  08:32 AEDT, 30 October 2026   |  Updated:  08:32 AEDT, 30 October 2026

A beloved art professor and his wife were allegedly murdered by their son in Ohio, police said.

Pipo Nguyen-Duy, who taught studio art and photography at Oberlin College and Conservatory, was found dead along with his wife Thi Tran Phong, 56, inside a home near the college.

Police said they were led to the crime scene after they responded to a call to the conservatory's parking lot to help Oberlin Fire with a vehicle that appeared to be on fire on Wednesday morning.

When crews arrived on scene, they tried to locate the registered vehicle owner, identified as Daniel Jones, Fox 8 reported.

When the 31-year-old suspect was not found, the police went to his home to conduct a welfare check.

Inside the house, the 64-year-old professor was found dead on the first floor, while his wife was on the second floor. Both the victims died of multiple gunshot wounds, police said.

Jones, Nguyen-Duy’s son and Phong's stepson, was later located in Shipherd Circle, a mile away from the crime scene.

The Oberlin police took the suspect into custody. He was charged with six counts of murder, four counts of felonious assault and one count of tampering with evidence, Cleveland 19 reported.

Studio art and photography professor, Pipo Nguyen-Duy was found dead along with his wife Thi Tran Phong inside a home near Oberlin College and Conservatory

Daniel Jones, Nguyen-Duy’s son, was the prime suspect in the murder. He was arrested by the Oberlin police and was charged with six counts of murder

The 64-year-old professor was found dead on the first floor, while his wife was on the second floor. Both the victims died of multiple gunshot wounds

‘I don’t know what could have transpired for someone to do that. I mean, to me he didn’t seem like he had a mean bone in his body,’ Shawn Stovall, a friend and neighbor of Nguyen-Duy, told Fox 8.

Jones had earlier told residents that he was trying to escape from a cult a few days before the alleged murders, the outlet reported.

‘He had tattoos on his forehead and his face. He looked wet and very disheveled, very nervous. He had a fanny pack or some kind of backpack that they’re looking for right now because they think that’s where the murder weapon is,’ Greg Poirson, an Oberlin resident said.

Daniel Jones's initial court appearance took place on Thursday at Lorain County Common Pleas Court. Jones did not enter a plea yet.

His bond was initially set for $1.5 million but Oberlin Municipal Court Judge Farah Emeka asked to double it 'given the egregious nature of the charges, WKYC reported.

The Oberlin College and Conservatory issued a shelter-in-place order after the police informed them of the incident.

The police lifted the order after it was confirmed there was no threat to the campus or community.

Katherine Pahal, an Oberlin student, told Cleveland 19 that she smelled smoke before getting the alert.

‘We knew something was up, but we didn’t know what it was,' Pahal said. ‘It wasn’t until maybe a half-hour later that we got the call and e-mail telling us to shelter in place but still it didn’t tell us what was happening, just that something was happening.’

Oberlin College President Carmen Twillie Ambar later sent a note to students, informing them about the professor’s death.

‘This is a deeply challenging moment for our campus. I am writing to share the tragic news of the violent passing of Pipo Nguyen-Duy. Tragedies such as this one intrude upon our lives in jarring ways. I am simply overwhelmed with sadness, and I am deeply concerned about the impact of the devastating loss of Pipo to our community.’

‘Pipo was beloved. During his years at Oberlin, he touched all of us through his passion for photography. In the days ahead, we will honor Pipo’s life. Our community will be hurting for a very long time.’

The professor was a native of Vietnam and had immigrated to the US as a political refugee in 1975.

He won many prominent awards, including a Guggenheim Fellowship and residencies. He had taught at the university since 1998.

The next hearing date has not yet been publicly scheduled following Jones' grand jury bind-over.
